title: This Ancient Croc Cousin Walked Like a Dinosaur—and Had a Beak!
summary:
Picture a crocodile. Now, forget everything you know! A newly discovered ancient reptile called Labrujasuchus expectatus looked nothing like today's crocs. It walked on two legs, had short little arms, and no teeth—just a beak, like an ostrich. But here's the twist: it's actually a relative of crocodiles! 

This bizarre creature lived during the Triassic Period, about 200 million years ago. Back then, animals were trying out all sorts of weird body shapes. Labrujasuchus belonged to a group called shuvosaurs, which were croc cousins that evolved to look like dinosaurs. Scientists call this convergent evolution—when unrelated animals end up with similar features because they live similar lives. 

The fossil was found at Ghost Ranch in New Mexico, a famous spot for Triassic fossils. Its name is a mix of local legend and science: Labrujasuchus honors Ranchos de los Brujos (Ranch of the Witches), an old Spanish name for the area, and suchus means crocodile in Greek. The species name expectatus means expected, because scientists had predicted a fossil like this would fill a gap in the evolutionary timeline. 

Only five shuvosaur species are known, so this find is a big deal. It helps paleontologists understand how crocodile relatives experimented with different body plans long before dinosaurs took over. Dr. Alan Turner, who led the study, says bipedalism—walking on two legs—was a unique path for croc relatives, but it clearly worked for these animals. 

Ghost Ranch continues to be a treasure trove. Every summer, paleontologists and volunteers dig there, uncovering more pieces of Earth's strange prehistoric past. Who knows what other odd creatures are still waiting to be found?
why_it_matters: Learning about strange prehistoric animals like Labrujasuchus helps us understand how all life, including crocodiles, birds, and even people, is connected through evolution.

The Triassic Period was a time long before dinosaurs became the main land animals; all kinds of unusual reptiles were experimenting with different body shapes.
Paleontologists have been digging at Ghost Ranch for many years, uncovering clues about how life evolved on Earth.
